claims.statement: The aggregate dashboard backend router has prefix "/dashboard/api" and a router-level same-origin mutation dependency; create_app includes it before mounting the dashboard UI.

openswe.dashboard exposes its router lazily through PEP 562 __getattr__, so importing dashboard submodules does not load routes.py, FastAPI, and all feature modules unless the web application mounts the router.

GitHub login signs state containing a hash of a nonce stored in a state cookie; the ordinary callback validates that nonce, exchanges the code, gates and persists the GitHub identity, and issues a session cookie, while a desktop handoff returns a PKCE-bound code without setting that browser cookie.

Session cookie flags derive from API scheme and dashboard/API origin relationship: HTTP is non-Secure SameSite=Lax, same-origin HTTPS is Secure SameSite=Lax, and split-origin HTTPS is Secure SameSite=None.

Every dashboard mutation is guarded by the router-level same-origin dependency: safe methods and bearer-token-only requests pass, cookie-authenticated mutations require an allowed Origin or Referer, and WebSockets always receive the origin check.
require_session decodes the osw_session cookie or raises 401, while endpoints requiring administration use an additional admin dependency.
The browser dashboard fetch layer uses a relative /dashboard/api base so browser calls remain same-origin, while SSR uses DASHBOARD_API_URL and forwards the incoming cookie header explicitly.

The deployed Nitro backend proxy reads DASHBOARD_API_URL per request, refuses to use an unset backend, preserves OAuth redirects with redirect: manual, and forwards each Set-Cookie as a separate response header.

The experimental Electron app ships the compiled web UI at open-swe://app and proxies dashboard API requests to a configured compatible backend, so the renderer does not call raw LangGraph directly; packaged builds have no hosted backend default.

Electron's legacy BackendSupervisor lazily starts an authenticated LangGraph server bound to 127.0.0.1 from langgraph.desktop.json in development or bundled configuration when packaged, passing a project allowlist, worktree directory, and external artifact/checkpoint locations.

The local-graph proxy removes renderer cookies, injects the supervisor's random bearer token, exposes stable /local-graph agent configuration, polls the token-authenticated loopback server at startup, and escalates shutdown from SIGTERM to SIGKILL after its timeout.

The backend dashboard UI mount serves a configured or in-repository static build at the root, gives assets immutable caching and the shell no-cache, declines reserved and non-HTML unknown paths, and can instead reverse-proxy a Vite development server while retaining the backend origin.
The dashboard UI catch-all must be registered after API routes, and keep_dashboard_ui_last moves it behind routes registered later.
At application construction, DASHBOARD_ALLOWED_ORIGINS configures credentialed CORS, wildcard origins are rejected, and the Electron open-swe://app origin is allowed.

POST /auth/desktop/exchange redeems a desktop handoff only with its verifier and returns the session value with its expiry; both Electron and oswe login use a loopback callback and retain the PKCE verifier locally.
The React router takes its basepath from Vite BASE_URL and configures generated routes, SSR query integration, scroll restoration, intent preloading, and pre-navigation thread-load timing.

The thread API provides authorized listing, detail, state, commands, run, history, diff and file surfaces; all=true discovery is admin-only and machine principals follow distinct machine-thread paths.

POST /threads/{thread_id}/stream/events forwards an authorized request to the thread proxy and returns an SSE response with no-cache and keep-alive headers; the commands endpoint is the common start/continue entry point for dashboard, API-key, and federated-workflow clients.

Dashboard thread creation resolves model and effort from workspace defaults, profile settings, and valid explicit choices, applies a vision fallback for image input, stamps ownership, visibility, participant, repository, workspace and resolved-model metadata, and appends a transcript creation event only when PostgreSQL is configured.
Workspace settings are layered: sparse workspace records inherit missing fields from an instance record, while profile and thread configuration can layer above them in supporting callers.
Electron's preload exposes a constrained openSweDesktop IPC surface for desktop operations rather than Node or Electron internals directly to the renderer.

Electron LocalBridges opens one bridge per This Mac thread, preserves the backend-assigned bridge ID for reopening, serves the checkout with the user's shell environment, and closes all active bridges when the application exits.

The CLI resolves credentials in API-key, GitHub Actions OIDC, explicit-session, then stored-session order; API-key and OIDC identities are machine credentials, while session credentials send osw_session with the backend Origin.

oswe run opens a bridge for the current directory, permits resume only for a remembered matching directory and non-conflicting bridge, stamps bridge and repository context only on a new thread, starts the run through the dashboard commands endpoint, follows its SSE stream, and cleans up the bridge on completion or cancellation.

The CLI SSE collector filters replayed stream data to the current top-level run, captures cli_result tool input, and retries closed retryable streams with exponential backoff; a healthy minute resets its budget and more than ten consecutive reconnects stops following.

oswe tools and oswe tool discover and invoke the backend CLI MCP catalog, while oswe mcp serves MCP on stdio; their documented tool operations require a person's session rather than machine credentials.

Focused CLI tests cover bridges, commands, configuration, credential/input handling, MCP behavior, and stream parsing; desktop tests cover backend supervision, configuration/login, preload, stores, worktree Git behavior, terminals, and update state.
